vulnerability.name: In-memory bash history artefact
vulnerability.author: Thomas Shaw
vulnerability.description: A detached interactive shell is left running with a command in its history that carries a token. The shell's HISTFILE is pointed away from disk, so the command never reaches ~/.bash_history and survives only in the running shell's memory. It is recoverable from a RAM image by searching the raw capture (strings), not from any file on disk. Teaches that an interactive shell keeps its command history in memory, separate from the on-disk history file.
vulnerability.hint: An interactive shell remembers the commands you typed even when it is told not to write them to a file.
vulnerability.solution: Search a RAM capture for the command in the running shell's in-memory history (strings on the image); the command carrying the token is not in any on-disk history file.
